context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining data consistency. It enables online submissions, fast adjuster processing, and incremental claim type migration over a 3-year period.

## Key Elements
* **Users:** Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters, and Finance/Compliance Auditors.
* **Modern Claims Platform (Azure West Europe):** Hosts the online portal, Adjuster Web App, Reporting & Reconciliation Service, and Transactional Outbox.
* **Legacy Mainframe Claims System (On-Premises):** COBOL/DB2 system acting as the enduring system of record.
* **Identity Provider:** Insurer's Active Directory / Azure AD.

## Relationships
* **Customer/Broker -> Modern Claims Platform:** HTTPS (Web/UI) for online claim submission.
* **Claims Adjuster -> Modern Claims Platform:** HTTPS for claim handling with sub-2s response times.
* **Modern Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe:** Asynchronous message bus (MQ/Kafka) via Site-to-Site VPN / Azure ExpressRoute secured with Mutual TLS (mTLS).
* **Modern Claims Platform -> Identity Provider:** OIDC/OAuth 2.0 with MFA for Single Sign-On (R-07).

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud Infrastructure:** Azure App Service / AKS (Azure West Europe) chosen for managed services to offset limited cloud experience.
* **Integration & Consistency:** Asynchronous message broker with Transactional Outbox Pattern for zero-loss claim migration (R-04).
* **Performance & Caching:** Read-aside caching in the modern platform to bypass 5-second mainframe latency and meet sub-2s adjuster requirements (R-05).
* **Security & Compliance:** Azure Key Vault for secrets management; AES-256 encryption at rest; append-only storage for audit log integrity.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the user-facing web tier from legacy mainframe latency while strictly adhering to the 3-year system-of-record constraint and interface change limits. Incremental claim migration and read-aside caching ensure fast adjuster response times and rapid 24-hour rollback capabilities.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system incrementally modernizes a legacy regional insurance claims platform by migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud architecture. It maintains operational continuity and zero data loss while interacting with an on-premise mainframe.

## Key Elements
- **Users:** Customer, Broker, Claims Adjuster, Finance/Compliance Auditor
- **External Systems:** Legacy Mainframe Claims System, Azure Active Directory (Identity Provider)
- **Containers:** 
  - API Gateway (Azure API Management)
  - Customer Portal & Adjuster Web App (Azure Container Apps / React)
  - Claims Domain Services (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
  - Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Service Bus)
  - Claims Audit Store (Azure Cosmos DB)
  - Mainframe Adapter (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)

## Relationships
- Customer/Broker/Adjuster/Auditor to API Gateway via HTTPS (TLS 1.3) with OpenID Connect (OIDC) JWT tokens
- API Gateway to Customer Portal, Adjuster Web App, and Claims Domain Services via HTTPS
- Claims Domain Services to Claims Audit Store via HTTPS (Document API)
- Claims Domain Services to Integration Layer via AMQP (Azure Service Bus)
- Integration Layer to Mainframe Adapter via AMQP
- Mainframe Adapter to Legacy Mainframe via custom TCP/LU6.2 bridging over Azure ExpressRoute/IPsec VPN with mTLS

## Technology Stack
- **Compute:** Azure Container Apps for abstracting Kubernetes complexity for the cloud-inexperienced team
- **Frontend:** React for responsive UI meeting the sub-2s performance constraint
- **Backend & Integration:** .NET Core for domain microservices and legacy adapters
- **Messaging:** Azure Service Bus with transactional outbox pattern to respect batch windows and ensure zero data loss
- **Database:** Azure Cosmos DB for append-only, immutable business event auditing and PII encryption
- **Security:** Azure API Management and Azure AD for SSO and RBAC enforcement

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates domains to enable independent claim type migration and rapid one-day rollbacks. It protects legacy mainframe constraints while leveraging managed Azure services to minimize cloud operational overhead.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Insurance Claims Modernization platform using a hybrid architecture to gradually migrate a 30-year-old mainframe to Azure.]
[Core Purpose: Enable online claim submission and adjuster processing while maintaining data consistency and legacy integration.]

## Key Elements
• API Gateway: Azure API Management
• Frontends: Customer Portal & Adjuster Web App (Azure Container Apps, React)
• Backend Services: Claims Domain Services, Mainframe Adapter (Azure Container Apps, .NET Core)
• Integration: Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Service Bus)
• Storage: Claims Audit Store (Azure Cosmos DB)
• Security: Active Directory / Identity Provider

## Relationships
• Customer / Broker / Adjuster -> API Gateway: Sends API requests and accesses portals/web app [HTTPS (TLS 1.3) with OIDC JWT tokens]
• API Gateway -> Claims Domain Services: Routes traffic and invokes services [gRPC over mTLS]
• API Gateway -> Mainframe Adapter: Integrates with legacy system [gRPC over mTLS]
• Claims Domain Services -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes integration events [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
• Azure API Management: Centralizes security, rate-limiting, and routing (R-07)
• Azure Container Apps: Hosts scalable microservices and web frontends with low cloud expertise overhead
• .NET Core: Powers robust domain services and mainframe adapters
• Azure Cosmos DB: Stores audit logs and compliance views with high availability
• gRPC over mTLS: Secures internal service-to-service communication with minimal latency

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while delivering sub-2-second adjuster response times via Azure caching and API management.]
[It guarantees zero claim loss and seamless single sign-on integration through modern cloud-native patterns.]

Customer Portal & Adjuster Web App.analysis:
## Overview
[The Customer Portal & Adjuster Web App modernizes user interactions for a regional insurer's claims platform. It provides responsive web interfaces for customers, brokers, and claims adjusters while hiding legacy mainframe latencies.]

## Key Elements
- SPA Shell & Routing Engine (React / TypeScript)
- Dynamic Form Engine (React Hook Form / JSON Schema)
- Optimistic UI & Local State Cache (TanStack Query)
- Telemetry & Error Boundary Handler (Azure Application Insights SDK)

## Relationships
- Browser to Azure API Management Gateway: Routes client traffic [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- SPA Shell to Azure Active Directory: Authenticates users and manages sessions [OpenID Connect / OIDC]
- Telemetry Handler to Azure Application Insights: Streams anonymized performance metrics and error logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React with TypeScript: Chosen for team familiarity and rich ecosystem supporting component-driven UI.
- JSON Schema & React Hook Form: Enables dynamic, metadata-driven form rendering to support iterative claim type migration without frontend deployments.
- TanStack Query: Manages local state and caching to meet sub-2-second performance requirements despite mainframe lag.
- Azure Container Apps: Hosts the frontend application within the hybrid cloud architecture.

## Rationale
[This component-level architecture ensures sub-2-second UI performance and dynamic metadata rendering to support iterative claim migrations. It strictly enforces security, RBAC, and OIDC authentication against the insurer's Active Directory.]

Claims Domain Services.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance mainframe by gradually migrating claims handling to a hybrid cloud platform while legacy processing continues. It ensures zero claim loss, sub-2-second adjuster screens, and rapid one-day rollback capabilities.]

## Key Elements
- Claim Orchestrator Component (.NET Core / Mediator pattern)
- Claim Domain Model Component (.NET Core)
- Rollback Switch Component (.NET Core / Feature Flag pattern)
- Claim Audit & Event Publisher Component (.NET Core / Outbox Pattern)
- Azure Container Apps (.NET Core runtime)
- Azure Cosmos DB (Claims Audit Store)
- Azure Service Bus (Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer)
- Azure Key Vault (Secrets and CMK management)

## Relationships
- Claim Orchestrator -> Claim Domain Model: In-memory domain method calls [Direct]
- Claim Orchestrator -> Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer: Publishes domain events [AMQP (Azure Service Bus)]
- Rollback Switch -> Mainframe Adapter: Forwards unmigrated claim traffic [gRPC with payload signing]
- Claim Domain Model -> Claim Audit & Event Publisher: Raises domain events [In-memory / MediatR]
- Claim Audit & Event Publisher -> Claims Audit Store: Persists audit records [HTTPS (Document API)]
- Claim Audit & Event Publisher -> Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer: Dispatches integration events [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- .NET Core: Selected for high-performance domain logic and microservice development
- Azure Container Apps: Chosen for serverless container orchestration with minimal cloud management overhead
- Azure Service Bus: Provides reliable asynchronous messaging using AMQP
- Azure Cosmos DB: Stores audit events with high availability and consistency
- Azure Key Vault: Secures PII encryption keys and managed identities

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples modern claim processing from the legacy mainframe using CQRS and the Outbox pattern, ensuring high performance and data consistency. The componentized design enforces strict security boundaries and supports the required 3-year hybrid coexistence and rapid rollback capabilities.]

Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern Azure-hosted platform while maintaining hybrid coexistence.]

## Key Elements
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Service Bus)
- Message Router Component (.NET Core / Azure Service Bus Topics)
- Translation & Mapping Component (.NET Core)
- Crypto-Proxy Middleware (.NET Core)
- Dead Letter & Audit Store Component (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Replay & Reconciliation Component (.NET Core / Azure Functions)
- Mainframe Adapter (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)

## Relationships
- Claims Domain Services -> Message Router: Publishes domain events [AMQP (Azure Service Bus)]
- Message Router -> Translation & Mapping: Transforms payloads [In-memory / .NET]
- Translation & Mapping -> Crypto-Proxy Middleware: Encrypts/decrypts sensitive payloads [In-memory / .NET]
- Translation & Mapping -> Mainframe Adapter: Dispatches legacy messages [AMQP]
- Replay & Reconciliation -> Message Router: Re-queues corrected messages [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous messaging and transactional outbox pattern to ensure zero data loss.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Provides immutable storage and customer-managed encryption keys for auditability and dead-letter management.
- .NET Core / Azure Functions: Powers routing, mapping, cryptographic proxying, and replay components.
- Azure Key Vault Managed HSMs: Secures cryptographic keys with automated rotation.

## Rationale
[This architecture ensures zero data loss and supports seamless one-day claim type rollbacks during the 3-year hybrid migration. It isolates legacy schemas while enforcing strict security and compliance controls.]

Claims Audit Store.analysis:
## Overview
- Architecture summary for the Claims Audit Store within the hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform.
- Provides tamper-proof, compliant event sourcing and long-term audit logging during the 3-year mainframe migration.

## Key Elements
- Claims Audit Store (Azure Cosmos DB): Append-only, immutable database container.
- Audit Event Writer (.NET Core / Cosmos SDK): Component handling PII tokenization and persistence.
- Compliance Query Service (.NET Core): Component providing secure, role-based query endpoints for auditors.
- Cosmos DB Change Feed Processor (.NET Core): Component powering asynchronous projections and archival triggers.
- Audit Archival Worker (Azure Function / .NET Core): Component moving historical logs to cold storage.
- Azure Blob Storage: Long-term WORM-compliant storage tier for 7-year retention.
- Azure Key Vault: Manages Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) and encryption keys.

## Relationships
- Claims Domain Services -> Audit Event Writer: Writes domain events via HTTPS (Document API)
- Finance/Compliance Auditors -> Compliance Query Service: Queries audit reports via HTTPS with Azure Active Directory SSO (R-07)
- Cosmos DB Change Feed Processor -> Audit Archival Worker: Triggers historical data offloading via internal Azure messaging
- Audit Archival Worker -> Azure Blob Storage: Archives immutable logs via HTTPS (Blob REST API)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API & Analytical Store): Selected for low latency (R-05) and change feed capabilities.
- .NET Core: Used for containerized microservices and workers due to team familiarity.
- Azure Blob Storage (Cool/Archive tier with WORM): Provides cost-effective 7-year regulatory retention.
- Azure Key Vault: Secures data at rest via Customer-Managed Keys (CMK).
- Azure Monitor / Log Analytics: Generates immutable read-access audit logs.

## Rationale
- This architecture guarantees zero data loss and strict consistency (R-04) through immutable event storage and strict access controls. It offloads historical data to meet 7-year retention rules without impacting sub-second adjuster performance (R-05).

Mainframe Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system via a hybrid cloud platform while ensuring uninterrupted legacy operations. The core purpose is to migrate claim types incrementally without risking data loss or exceeding strict mainframe change budgets.]

## Key Elements
* Customer Portal & Adjuster Web App (Azure Container Apps / React)
* API Gateway (Azure API Management)
* Claims Domain Services (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Service Bus)
* Mainframe Adapter Container (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* Request Translator Component (.NET Core)
* LU6.2 Protocol Bridge Component (C#/.NET native sockets)
* Outbox & State Cache Component (Entity Framework Core / Redis)
* Telemetry & Audit Emitter Component (.NET Core / OpenTelemetry)
* Claims Audit Store (Azure Cosmos DB)
* Legacy Mainframe Claims System (COBOL/DB2 on-premise)
* Identity Provider (Active Directory)

## Relationships
* Adjuster Web App -> API Gateway: Forwards user actions [HTTPS/REST]
* API Gateway -> Claims Domain Services: Routes validated API requests [HTTPS/gRPC]
* Claims Domain Services -> Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer: Publishes claim events [AMQP]
* Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Mainframe Adapter: Transfers integration messages [AMQP]
* Request Translator -> LU6.2 Protocol Bridge: Invokes in-memory message mapping [Direct]
* LU6.2 Protocol Bridge -> Legacy Mainframe Claims System: Transmits framed byte arrays [Custom TCP/LU6.2 over mTLS / ExpressRoute]
* Telemetry & Audit Emitter -> Claims Audit Store: Persists audit logs [HTTPS/Cosmos SDK]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Container Apps: Hosts microservices with low cloud experience overhead
* .NET Core: Powers backend domain services and mainframe adapter components
* Redis & Entity Framework Core: Implements transactional outbox pattern and state caching
* Azure Service Bus: Asynchronously decouples cloud services from the legacy mainframe
* Custom TCP/LU6.2 over ExpressRoute/IPsec VPN: Bridges modern cloud architecture to legacy mainframe
* Azure Cosmos DB: Stores tamper-evident transaction audits and compliance logs

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture bridges modern cloud services with a legacy mainframe while strictly adhering to integration and performance constraints. Internal component decomposition guarantees high-performance adjuster UI responses despite slow legacy lag and provides a rapid rollback mechanism.]
